references.text: Repeats the prohibition against leaving any of the Passover lamb until morning, specifying that it must be eaten in one house without breaking any bones.
The command that fat from the festival offering must not remain until the next morning, paralleling the treatment of the Passover lamb.
The consecration offering was also to be burned if anything remained until morning, following the same principle as for the Passover lamb.
The meat of the thank offering was to be eaten on the same day and not left until the next morning, a similar rule to that for the Passover lamb.
The thank offering was to be eaten on the same day without anything being left until morning.
The regulations for the Passover lamb are repeated, including that nothing must remain until morning.
The meat from the Passover offering must not remain until the next morning, confirming the rule from Exodus 2.
John refers to the regulations of the Passover lamb and their fulfillment in Christ as the true Passover lamb.
Leviticus 8:32 confirms and expands on the rule from Exodus 29 that any remainder of the consecration offering must be burned.
Contrasts with Exodus 12 by showing that other offerings have a longer time frame before the remains must be burned.
